picks.title: China’s Smart Glasses Are Once Again Making Meta Look Silly
picks.excerpt: Alibaba's Qwen Glasses N1 smart glasses make lofty claims about battery life and have a camera sensor that crushes Meta on paper.
picks.rationale: Alibaba's Qwen Glasses N1 is a new AI-glasses launch built around its own Qwen model, and on paper its camera and battery beat Meta's. It is a new competitor in the busiest AI-wearable category.

picks.title: With 16 TOPS, NVMe support, and SATA, the new OrangePi O1 makes the Raspberry Pi look dated
picks.excerpt: Boasting 16 TOPS of hardware AI acceleration and extensive connectivity, the OrangePi O1 single-board computer looks set to give the Raspberry Pi serious competition for edge AI workloads.
picks.rationale: The OrangePi O1 is a new single-board computer with a 16 TOPS NPU and NVMe/SATA storage, aimed at edge-AI work. It is cheap hardware a maker or prototyper can build local-AI projects on now.

picks.title: UCLA researchers built a $400 humanoid robot around cheap phone technology
picks.excerpt: This open-source humanoid robot walks, tracks people, and gets back up using inexpensive hardware and a smartphone instead of dedicated sensors
picks.rationale: UCLA's open-source PhoneBot uses a $50 Android phone as the brain and eyes of a $400 humanoid that walks, tracks people and gets back up on its own. It brings embodied AI down to maker budgets.

picks.title: Nothing reportedly launching two pairs of smart glasses, one with barely any AI
picks.excerpt: A reliable source says that Nothing is building out its own AI smart glasses that feature ChatGPT integration, a camera,...
picks.rationale: A report says Nothing is building two pairs of glasses: one with ChatGPT integration and a camera, and one with almost no AI. That split is a useful product-design signal about how much AI a wearable should carry. Copy must make clear this is a report, not a launch.

picks.title: The Pixel 11 Pro’s 120x zoom is ridiculous, but is it actually useful?
picks.excerpt: The Pixel 11 Pro pushes Pro Res Zoom to 120x, up from 100x on the Pixel 10 Pro, combining a brighter telephoto camera with generative AI to reconstruct detail. Android Authority tests whether it is actually useful.
picks.rationale: A field test of Pixel 11 Pro's 120x Pro Res Zoom, where generative AI rebuilds detail that the optics never captured. It shows when AI-reconstructed photos can be trusted, which matters to anyone shooting reference images on a phone.

alternates.title: 사람과 무술 대결하는 로봇…공중제비에 발차기까지
alternates.excerpt: 중국 로봇 스타트업 애지봇은 자사 휴머노이드 로봇 'A3'가 액션 배우들과 함께 쿵푸 동작을 선보이는 영상을 공개했습니다.
alternates.rationale: AgiBot's A3 kung-fu humanoid video. It is new, but it would be a second humanoid card next to the UCLA PhoneBot. First alternate.

alternates.title: Apple's next HomeView could debut as soon as next year with a robotic arm: report
alternates.excerpt: Apple just announced its long awaited smart home display: HomeView, and it's available for $299.
alternates.rationale: A rumor about a future robotic-arm HomeView. It sits close to the HomeView launch card from 10-14 (nearest: arstechnica HomeView). Second alternate only; it needs a new dedup check if it is swapped in.
